Some time ago I installed Ubuntu Server on a spare computer with the goal of turning it into a private home server. Currently it is mostly used for streaming purposes which does not really utilize the server completely.

I currently got CouchPotato, SickBeard, Plex, Sabnzbd and a torrent downloader running.

Quick overview of specs: Q8400 @ 2.66GHz 8GB RAM 2TB HDD 120GB SSD

Nothing blazingly fast but way too powerful for what I am currently using the server for. For example: on average the server uses 700MB ram and has a hard time maxing out one of the four cores on the CPU.

This got me thinking about what else I can use this server for. All this spare processing power is now just going to wast. Surely I can do something more fun/useful with it!

Anybody got an idea what else I can do with it?
Help me decide what to do with my too powerful Ubuntu server

I recommend joining a BOINC project of your taste. *Coin mining is mainly done with ASICs nowadays as it outperforms CPUs and GPUs by a magnitude. Edit: Antminer S7 is about 1000 times as efficient as a high end graphics card. So buy specific mining hardware if you intend on mining coins.
Interesting. I had not seriously considered using my spare computer for this purpose before. Seems like a good cause and it's not like I am going to use the processing power anyway.
Install a hypervisor on it to make it run more servers
Apart from this being pretty awesome are there any practical applications to this?

If you are using this as an HTPC, you can use the hypervisor to hold an Android x86 instance. In theory this is the first step to chromecasting to your linux box and using a bunch of cool android apps, but honestly its not simple.
Mumble or Jitsi. However I would go with visualization so you have better control.

Here are some ideas:

  1. You like free Software and want to do something for the community? Community projects like Debian and Fedora are always looking for volunteers who can help them with server resources. All you need is a static url or an IPAddress, they will route a lot of downloaders to your server, and it will be utilized.
  2. Like someone here said, you can use it for Bitcoin/Litecoin mining, though considering its specs I don't think you will be able to make much after subtracting power bills.
  3. You need a place to host files and folders on the go? Sure, there is Dropbox and Google drive, but if you any tech-savvy, you will love the idea of self-hosting.
  4. Are you a programmer? Turn your server into a git server. Unlike hosting on Github, you won't have to pay any fees for private repos since you are hosting on your own server!

Host your own file server. I use pydio, but other people use syncthing or seafile or whatever. Its nice to be able to access all of your files, movies, music, etc. while on-the-go.

Its also nice to set up an OpenSSH server. You can mount an OpenSSH server from over the web and use the files as though they were on a very, very slow hard drive.

It goes without saying, if you do this you must establish RSA/SSL wherever appropriate. Never give Apache webserver root permissions, that is a really dangerous work-around.
